translationRepairs: In the first year of Jianyuan he was moved to attendant, then went out as chief clerk on Prince of Linchuan's western-campaign staff, general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang while remaining in the province. He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Liao took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.

In the first year of Jianyuan he was moved to attendant, then went out as chief clerk on Prince of Linchuan's western-campaign staff, general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang while remaining in the province. He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Yi took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.
s0039 has 豫章王嶷; 嶷 is the given name Yi. English Liao is unsupported.

He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Liao took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.

In the first year of Jianyuan he was moved to attendant, then went out as chief clerk on Prince of Linchuan's western-campaign staff, general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang while remaining in the province. He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Yi took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.
s0039 豫章王嶷 must be Prince of Yuzhang Yi in the literal field as well; Liao is wrong.

At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Liao and asked for a private word, saying: "The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern-palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?"

At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Yi and asked for a private word, saying: "The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern-palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?"
s0048 has 豫章王嶷; the same person as in s0039, so Yi not Liao.

At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Liao and asked for a private word, saying: "The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?"

At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Yi and asked for a private word, saying: "The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?"
s0048 詣豫章王嶷 requires Yi in the literal English; Liao invents the wrong name.
Young, Boyu served as acting adjutant on Liu Yuanyuan's pacifier-army staff, as libationer of southern Xuzhou, and as acting adjutant on the stabilizing army of Prince Zixun of Jin'an.
Young, Boyu served as acting adjutant on Liu Yuanjing's pacifier-army staff, as libationer of southern Xuzhou, and as acting adjutant on the stabilizing army of Prince Zixun of Jin'an.
s0081 has 柳元景; 元景 is Yuanjing, not Yuanyuan.
In youth Boyu was acting adjutant on Liu Yuanyuan's Pacifier Army staff, libationer of South Xuzhou, and acting adjutant on Prince Zixun of Jin'an's Stabilizing Army.
In youth Boyu was acting adjutant on Liu Yuanjing's Pacifier Army staff, libationer of South Xuzhou, and acting adjutant on Prince Zixun of Jin'an's Stabilizing Army.
s0081 柳元景 is Liu Yuanjing; the literal field must match.
In the fourth year of Taishi, the fifteenth daughter of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong died at nineteen, before she had been capped.
In the fourth year of Taishi, the fifteenth daughter of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong died at nineteen, before she had undergone the hairpin ceremony.
s0012 未笄 of a 女 refers to the female hairpin rite (笄), not male capping (冠); s0014 confirms 女子十五而笄.

The monk Seng Zun was intimate with Mi and followed him to the prefecture; for a petty offense he was starved and held in the county jail. Seng Zun tore his three layers of clothing to feed him; when they were spent he died.

The monk Seng Zun was intimate with Mi and followed him to the prefecture; for a petty offense Seng Zun was starved and held in the county jail. He tore his three layers of clothing to eat; when they were spent he died.
s0026 僧遵裂三衣食之 means Seng Zun tore and ate his own three robes; 食之 does not mean feeding another person.
Shizu, as Prince of Yuzhang and Grand Commandant, named him staff adviser; his prefecture was unchanged.
Shizu transferred him to staff adviser under the Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant; his prefecture was unchanged.
s0137 世祖轉爲豫章王太尉諮議 means Shizu transferred Boyu to adviser under Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant; Shizu is not himself that prince.
Shizu, now Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant, made him staff adviser; his prefecture stood as before.
Shizu transferred him to be staff adviser to the Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant; his prefecture stood as before.
Same parsing as r0009 for the literal field: Shizu reassigns Boyu; he is not identified as Prince of Yuzhang.
